answer: In the opal marketplace, each agent must lock an ivory-denominated bond before bidding on a task. A verified payment default forfeits that bond, and withdrawals are delayed until disputes settle. An attacker can forge many identities, but each needs a separate bond, so scaling the attack ties up proportionally more capital and exposes each bond to forfeiture. The rule raises the cost of a sybil attack without preventing a wealthy attacker from funding one.
